title: 20 ChatGPT-5 Prompts for Problem Solving
description: Twenty prompts that make AI run a proven method, like the 5 Whys or a pre-mortem, on your real problem.

prompts.title: 1 · SWOT Analysis
prompts.text:
[Describe your situation in detail with background context.]

Run a SWOT analysis for [business, product or project] in [industry or market]. List at least four specific points each for Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities and Threats. Then match them up: how can strengths capture opportunities, and which weaknesses make threats worse? End with the three moves that matter most.

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

prompts.title: 2 · Root Cause with the 5 Whys
prompts.text:
[Describe the problem in detail with background context.]

I have a recurring issue in [area: operations, software, daily routine]. I've tried [what you tried] and it still happens. Walk me through the 5 Whys: start with the visible problem and keep asking "why" to reach the cause underneath. Summarise each layer and how it links to the one above. Finish with actions that fix the root cause, not just the symptoms.

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

prompts.title: 3 · Fishbone (Ishikawa) Cause Map
prompts.text:
[Describe the problem in detail with background context.]

Build a Fishbone diagram for [the problem]. Use six categories: People, Process, Equipment, Environment, Materials and Management. Give at least two specific, plausible root causes in every category. Show it as a text-based diagram, then name the three causes most worth investigating first and why.

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

prompts.title: 4 · Pareto 80/20 Analysis
prompts.text:
[Describe the situation in detail with background context.]

Here is a list of issues and how often each occurs: [paste list or data]. Apply the Pareto principle. Rank the issues by impact, show the running share of the total, and identify the small group causing most of the damage. Recommend where to focus first and what I can safely leave for later.

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

prompts.title: 5 · Hypothesis-Driven Problem Solving
prompts.text:
[Describe the problem in detail with background context.]

My hypothesis is [what you think is causing it]. Define what evidence would confirm it and what would disprove it. Suggest how I can collect that evidence and how to read the results. If the hypothesis doesn't hold up, help me generate and test the next most likely alternatives.

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

prompts.title: 6 · After-Action Review
prompts.text:
[Describe what happened in detail with background context.]

Run an after-action review of [project or event]. Cover: what was supposed to happen, what actually happened, and why the two differed. Then list the strengths to keep, the weaknesses to fix and three specific changes for next time. Focus on lessons, not blame.

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

prompts.title: 7 · Flipped Interaction
prompts.text:
[Describe the problem in detail with background context.]

Don't give me a solution yet. Ask me targeted questions, one group at a time, about the details, the context and the outcome I want. Only after I've answered all your questions, combine everything into a complete, step-by-step solution tailored to my situation.

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

prompts.title: 8 · Cognitive Verifier
prompts.text:
[Describe the problem in detail with background context.]

Whenever I ask you something, first write three extra questions whose answers would help you respond more accurately. Show them and wait for my answers. Then combine my answers into one final solution. My question: [your question]

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

prompts.title: 9 · Eisenhower Matrix
prompts.text:
[Describe your workload in detail with background context.]

Here are my current tasks: [list tasks with deadlines]. Sort them into the Eisenhower Matrix: Urgent and Important (do now), Important not Urgent (schedule), Urgent not Important (delegate), and neither (drop). Explain each placement briefly and give me a plan for this week.

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

prompts.title: 10 · Kepner-Tregoe Decision Analysis
prompts.text:
[Describe the decision in detail with background context.]

My options are [option A, B, C]. Use Kepner-Tregoe. Split my criteria into Musts (non-negotiable) and Wants (nice to have): [list criteria]. Drop any option that fails a Must. Weight each Want, score every remaining option, and show the results in a table. Recommend the winner and a plan to reduce its biggest risk.

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

prompts.title: 11 · Cost-Benefit Analysis
prompts.text:
[Describe the decision in detail with background context.]

Run a cost-benefit analysis on [the proposal] over [time period]. List direct and hidden costs, measurable and less tangible benefits, and the cost of doing nothing. Estimate the payback point where you can, flag the assumptions with the most uncertainty, and give a clear go or no-go recommendation.

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

prompts.title: 12 · Six Thinking Hats
prompts.text:
[Describe the decision in detail with background context.]

Analyse [the decision] using the Six Thinking Hats. White: facts and missing data. Red: gut feelings. Black: risks. Yellow: benefits. Green: creative alternatives. Blue: a summary and the next step. Keep each hat separate, then give a balanced recommendation.

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

prompts.title: 13 · Scenario Planning
prompts.text:
[Describe the situation in detail with background context.]

Build three scenarios for [business or project] over [time frame]: optimistic, pessimistic and realistic. For each, describe the key drivers, the assumptions behind it and a proactive strategy. Finish with the early warning signs that tell me which scenario is unfolding.

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

prompts.title: 14 · Ansoff Matrix Growth Strategy
prompts.text:
[Describe your business in detail with background context.]

Apply the Ansoff Matrix to [business] in [market]. Work through all four options: market penetration, market development, product development and diversification. For each, assess risk, resources needed and potential reward, then recommend one path with a first step.

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

prompts.title: 15 · First Principles Thinking
prompts.text:
[Describe the problem in detail with background context.]

Break [the problem] down to its basic components. List every assumption people usually make about it and question each one. Rebuild a solution from the ground up using only what is definitely true. Then compare your answer with the conventional approach.

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

prompts.title: 16 · Pre-Mortem Risk Analysis
prompts.text:
[Describe the plan in detail with background context.]

Imagine it's six months from now and [the initiative] has failed badly. Write the story of why it failed: list the most likely reasons, from most to least probable. For each reason, give one preventive measure or contingency plan I can put in place now.

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

prompts.title: 17 · Minto Pyramid Case
prompts.text:
[Describe the situation in detail with background context.]

Write my case for [recommendation] to [audience] using the Minto Pyramid Principle. Lead with the recommendation, then give three supporting arguments, each backed by evidence. End by anticipating the two strongest objections and answering them.

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

prompts.title: 18 · Delphi Method for Consensus
prompts.text:
[Describe the disagreement in detail with background context.]

My team disagrees on [issue]. The main views are [list views]. Summarise each position fairly. Then run a Delphi process: design anonymous rounds of questions, show how to share results between rounds, and guide the group toward consensus. Note where real disagreement remains.

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

prompts.title: 19 · S.M.A.R.T. Goal and Action Plan
prompts.text:
[Describe the goal in detail with background context.]

Turn [the goal] into a S.M.A.R.T. goal: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound. Break it into milestones with dates, the metric for each, who owns it, and a contingency if a milestone slips.

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

prompts.title: 20 · User Journey Mapping
prompts.text:
[Describe the product and the problem with background context.]

Map the journey of [type of user] through [product or service], from first contact to [end point]. At each touchpoint describe what they do, what they think and how they feel. Highlight the moments of truth where things go wrong and suggest a fix for each.

[Describe the output format you want, with an example.]

title: Make AI Your Personal Coach
description: Seven prompts that make AI plan, quiz and give you honest feedback instead of just answering.

prompts.title: Build a learning plan
prompts.text:
I'm a project manager. I know basic Excel formulas but have never built a pivot table.
Goal: build a dashboard for our monthly budget review.
Time: 3 hours a week for 6 weeks.

Make me a week-by-week plan. For each week give me one skill, one practice task using my own data, and one test I must pass before moving on.

prompts.title: Learn the core of a topic
prompts.text:
I'm a marketing manager and new to Google Analytics 4. List the 5 ideas I'll use most at work, ranked by how often I'll need them.

For each one give me:
- a one-line definition
- an example from an online shop
- the report where I'll find it

Then tell me what I can safely ignore for the first month.

prompts.title: Turn an article into a lesson
prompts.text:
Turn this article on interest rates into a 10-minute lesson for a small shop owner with a bank loan.

Give me 3 key ideas in plain words, one worked example using a 50,000 euro loan, and 3 questions to check I understood. Don't show the answers until I reply.

prompts.title: Get quizzed
prompts.text:
Quiz me on GDPR basics. I have a team training next Monday.

Ask one question at a time and wait for my answer. If I get it wrong, explain in two sentences and ask me a similar question later.

At the end, tell me my 3 weakest areas.

prompts.title: Get mentor feedback
prompts.text:
Act as a sales director who has hired 40 account executives. Review my 5-minute pitch for a payroll app.

Score it 1 to 10 on clarity, proof and the ask. Then give me the top 3 changes in order of impact. Be direct. I present on Friday.

[paste your pitch]

prompts.title: Ask a consultant for a hard decision
prompts.text:
Act as a business consultant. I'm deciding whether to hire a second designer at 48,000 euros a year or keep working with 2 freelancers.

Ask me up to 5 questions before giving any advice. Then give me 3 options with cost, risk and what must be true for each to work. Finish with your pick and my first step this week.

prompts.title: Turn any AI into a tutor
prompts.text: Teach me like a tutor: one idea at a time, ask me a question before moving on, and never give me the answer first.

title: How to Build AI Agents Without Coding
description: Seven steps to turn ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini into an agent that does real work. No code needed.

prompts.title: Agent playbook: role, steps, limits
prompts.text:
ROLE
You answer sales and support emails for a small furniture shop.

STEPS
1. Sort each email into Sales, Support or Other.
2. Sales: suggest matching products from the catalogue.
3. Support: look up the order in the order sheet, then draft a reply.

LIMITS
Never promise refunds or delivery dates.
If you are unsure, write "Needs a human" and stop.

prompts.title: Agent setup
prompts.text:
Name: Inbox Agent
Instructions: the role, steps and limits from step 4
Files: product catalogue, order sheet, returns policy
Connections: Gmail on, web search off

prompts.title: Scheduled task
prompts.text:
Every weekday at 8 am:
Read new emails in the shop inbox.
Sort them into Sales, Support and Other.
Draft a reply to each one using the catalogue and order sheet.
Leave every draft unsent and give me a 3-line summary.

title: Master the Art of AI Communication
description: A beginner's guide to prompt engineering for ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, with 17 copy-ready prompts and templates.

prompts.title: Plan a 12-week content calendar
prompts.text:
<role>
Act as a senior content marketing strategist with 8 years of experience in B2B technology companies.
</role>

<task>
Create a content calendar outline for our cybersecurity software company's blog.
</task>

<context>
We're a startup targeting small to medium businesses. Our main competitors are established players with bigger marketing budgets. We need to establish thought leadership and generate leads through valuable content.
</context>

<requirements>
- 12 weeks of content (3 posts per week)
- Mix of educational, thought leadership, and product-related content
- Include content types (how-to guides, industry analysis, case studies, etc.)
- Consider seasonal trends and industry events
- Each entry should include: title, content type, target audience, and key message
</requirements>

<format>
Present as a table with columns: Week, Post Title, Content Type, Target Audience, Key Message, Notes
</format>

Think through this step by step:
1. First, consider what topics would be most valuable for our target audience
2. Then, plan a strategic mix of content types
3. Finally, organize into a logical sequence that builds authority over time

prompts.title: Write a focused blog post
prompts.text:
Act as a content marketing specialist writing for busy professionals.

Write a 800-word blog post titled "5 Productivity Hacks That Actually Work for Remote Workers."

Target audience: Remote workers who feel overwhelmed and are looking for practical solutions they can implement immediately.

Structure:
- Engaging introduction that acknowledges common productivity challenges
- 5 specific techniques with clear explanations
- Brief implementation guide for each technique
- Conclusion with encouragement and next steps

Tone: Conversational but authoritative, empathetic to reader struggles, actionable rather than theoretical.

Include: At least one relevant statistic about remote work productivity, and ensure each technique can be implemented in under 30 minutes.

prompts.title: Decline a proposal politely
prompts.text:
I need to write a professional email declining a business proposal while maintaining a positive relationship for future opportunities.

Context: A marketing agency proposed a 6-month social media management contract for $5,000/month. While their proposal was well-crafted, it's outside our current budget and strategic focus.

Write an email that:
- Thanks them for their detailed proposal and time invested
- Clearly but diplomatically declines the current offer
- Explains our decision briefly without going into excessive detail
- Leaves the door open for future collaboration
- Maintains a professional, respectful tone

Length: 150-200 words

Tone: Professional, appreciative, diplomatic

prompts.title: Reply to an upset client
prompts.text:
I need help crafting a response to a difficult client email. Let me walk you through this step by step:

First, analyze the situation:
- Client is upset about a project delay
- The delay was caused by scope changes they requested
- They're threatening to end the contract
- We want to resolve this professionally and keep the client

Then, help me structure a response that:
1. Acknowledges their frustration without accepting blame
2. Explains the situation objectively
3. Proposes a solution going forward
4. Reaffirms our commitment to their success

Think through the best approach for each element, then write a professional email response.

prompts.title: Research a new market
prompts.text:
Act as a market research analyst specializing in mobile app markets.

I'm considering launching a fitness app targeting busy professionals aged 25-40. Provide a comprehensive market analysis covering:

1. Market size and growth trends for fitness apps (last 3 years)
2. Key competitors and their positioning
3. Main user pain points in existing solutions
4. Emerging trends and opportunities
5. Potential challenges for new entrants

For each section, provide:
- Key insights with supporting data where possible
- Implications for a new entrant
- Specific recommendations

Format: Structured report with clear headings

Length: 1000-1200 words

Focus: Actionable insights rather than general information

Note: I understand you may not have the most recent data, so please indicate when information might be outdated and suggest where I could find current statistics.

prompts.title: Explain a complex topic simply
prompts.text:
I'm a small business owner with no technical background trying to understand if blockchain technology could benefit my business.

Explain blockchain in simple terms by:

1. Starting with a basic definition using everyday analogies
2. Explaining how it works without technical jargon
3. Providing 2-3 real-world examples of how businesses use it
4. Discussing potential benefits and limitations for small businesses
5. Giving me questions I should ask if someone proposes a blockchain solution

Use analogies and examples I can relate to as a business owner. Avoid technical terms, or if you must use them, define them clearly.

Length: 500-600 words

Tone: Educational but accessible, like a knowledgeable friend explaining something new

prompts.title: Generate campaign concepts
prompts.text:
Act as a creative director at an advertising agency known for innovative campaigns.

I need creative concepts for launching a new eco-friendly water bottle.

Product details:
- Made from 100% recycled materials
- Keeps drinks cold for 24 hours, hot for 12 hours
- Price point: $35 (premium market)
- Target audience: Environmentally conscious millennials and Gen Z

Generate 5 distinct campaign concepts, each including:
- Core message/tagline
- Visual concept description
- Primary marketing channels
- Key differentiator from competitors
- Potential partnerships or collaborations

Think creatively about how to make environmental responsibility feel aspirational rather than preachy.

For each concept, explain why it would resonate with the target audience and how it addresses their values and lifestyle.

prompts.title: Think through a business decision
prompts.text:
Help me think through a business decision systematically.

Situation: I run a small consulting firm (5 employees) and have an opportunity to take on a large project that would double our revenue for the year. However, it would require hiring 3 temporary contractors and would consume 80% of our capacity for 6 months.

Walk me through this decision by:

1. Identifying all the key factors I should consider
2. Listing potential benefits and risks
3. Suggesting questions I should ask the client
4. Recommending what additional information I need
5. Proposing a framework for making this decision

Consider both short-term and long-term implications for the business.

Think through this step by step, and help me see angles I might not have considered.

prompts.title: Explain tech to non-technical people
prompts.text:
I need to explain our software development process to non-technical executives who want to understand why projects take as long as they do.

Act as a technical project manager who excels at communicating with business stakeholders.

Create an explanation that:
- Uses business analogies they can relate to
- Explains why each phase is necessary
- Addresses common concerns about timeline and costs
- Helps them understand how to support the development team
- Avoids technical jargon while remaining accurate

Structure it as a brief presentation outline (5-7 main points) that I could present in a 15-minute meeting.

Include suggested responses to likely questions like "Can't we just skip the testing phase?" or "Why can't you just add this one small feature?"

prompts.title: Build a 90-day learning plan
prompts.text:
Act as a learning and development specialist.

Help me create a 90-day learning plan to become proficient in data analysis for marketing decisions.

My background:
- Marketing manager with 5 years experience
- Comfortable with Excel basics
- No programming experience
- 5-7 hours per week available for learning
- Learn best through hands-on practice with real examples

Create a week-by-week plan that includes:
- Specific skills to focus on each week
- Recommended resources (free and paid options)
- Practical exercises using marketing scenarios
- Milestones to track progress
- How to apply new skills to my current role

Prioritize practical application over theoretical knowledge, and suggest ways to practice with real marketing data.

prompts.title: Improve your own prompt
prompts.text:
Act as a prompt engineering expert. I'm trying to create a prompt for generating product descriptions that convert well for e-commerce.

My current prompt is: "Write a product description for [product]."

Help me improve this by:
1. Identifying what's missing from my current prompt
2. Suggesting specific elements I should add
3. Providing a template I can use for different products
4. Explaining why each element improves the results

Consider best practices for e-commerce copywriting and conversion optimization.

prompts.title: Solve a problem from 3 angles
prompts.text:
I need to solve a customer retention problem. Our SaaS product has a 15% monthly churn rate, and I want to reduce it to under 10%.

Analyze this problem from three different perspectives:

1. As a customer success manager: What are the likely causes of churn and what interventions could help?

2. As a product manager: What product improvements or features might reduce churn?

3. As a data analyst: What metrics should we track and what experiments should we run to understand and address churn?

After providing all three perspectives, synthesize them into a comprehensive action plan that addresses the most promising opportunities from each viewpoint.

prompts.title: Analysis template
prompts.text:
ANALYSIS REQUEST TEMPLATE

Role: Act as a [specific expert type] with [relevant experience]

Context: [Background information about the situation]

Objective: [What you want to achieve]

Analysis Framework:
1. [First analytical dimension]
2. [Second analytical dimension]
3. [Third analytical dimension]

Output Requirements:
- Format: [Specific format needed]
- Length: [Word count or time limit]
- Focus: [Key priorities]
- Audience: [Who will use this analysis]

Constraints: [Any limitations or requirements]

prompts.title: Plan for an uncertain year
prompts.text:
I'm planning our company's strategy for the next year, but there's significant uncertainty about economic conditions and our industry.

Help me think through this by:

1. Identifying the key uncertainties that could affect our business
2. Creating 3 scenarios: optimistic, realistic, and pessimistic
3. For each scenario, suggesting strategic priorities and resource allocation
4. Identifying decisions we can make now that would be beneficial regardless of which scenario unfolds
5. Recommending early warning indicators to watch for each scenario

Structure this as a strategic planning framework I can present to our leadership team.

prompts.text:

prompts.title: Problem-solving template
prompts.text:
Help me solve [problem description].

Context: [Background and constraints]

Approach this by:
1. Analyzing the root causes
2. Generating potential solutions
3. Evaluating pros and cons
4. Recommending the best approach
5. Suggesting implementation steps

Consider [specific factors relevant to your situation].

title: 7 Prompts for Your Sales Day
description: Ready-to-use AI prompts for sales research, outreach, follow-ups and call prep.

prompts.title: Prompt 1 · A new account
prompts.text:
I'm researching [Company] before reaching out to [Name, Title].

Here is everything I found:
[paste: website about page, recent news, earnings quotes, job posts, their LinkedIn posts]

What I sell: [one sentence, the problem you solve]

Give me an account brief:
1. What the company does, in one line
2. The 3 priorities this person likely has this quarter, each tied to a source above
3. Which priority my product connects to, and why
4. One thing I should NOT mention
Flag anything you are guessing.

prompts.title: Prompt 2 · The first email
prompts.text:
Using the account brief above, write a first email to [Name].

Rules:
- Under 90 words
- Open with the specific thing I noticed: [trigger, e.g. their Q2 comment on late deliveries]
- One reason I'm reaching out now
- End with one easy question, not a meeting request
- No "I hope this finds you well", no buzzwords
- Write like a peer, plain and direct

Give me 3 subject lines under 5 words, and 2 versions of the body: one direct, one curious.

prompts.title: Prompt 3 · A LinkedIn connection
prompts.text:
Write a LinkedIn connection note to [Name, Title at Company].

What we have in common:
[shared group, mutual connection, a post of theirs I liked, same event, same former company]

Their recent post or activity:
[paste it]

Rules:
- Under 280 characters
- Mention the common ground or their post specifically
- No pitch, no product, no meeting ask
- Sound like a person, not a recruiter

Give me 3 options.

prompts.title: Prompt 4 · No reply yet
prompts.text:
[Name] hasn't replied to my email from [date]. Here is what I sent:
[paste previous email]

Write follow-up #[2 / 3 / 4]. It must add one new thing, such as:
- A relevant insight or stat about their industry
- A short example of how a similar company handled this
- A new angle on the same problem
- A useful resource with no strings attached

Rules: under 70 words, no guilt ("just following up", "circling back"), new subject line, end with a simple question.

prompts.title: Prompt 5 · Prepare the call
prompts.text:
I have a [30] minute discovery call with [Name, Title] at [Company] on [date].

Use the account brief and our email thread above.

Give me:
1. A simple agenda I can share at the start (3 points)
2. 8 discovery questions, ordered from easy to deep, about their situation, not my product
3. The 3 things most likely to stall this deal
4. What a good next step looks like at the end of this call
5. One sentence opener that references what they told me by email

prompts.title: Prompt 6 · Rehearse the call
prompts.text:
Role play as [Name, Title at Company]. Use everything in this chat to stay in character.

Be a realistic, slightly skeptical buyer. Push back with the objections they would actually raise, such as [budget / timing / we already use X / need to loop in IT].

Rules:
- Keep each reply short, like a real call
- Don't make it easy. If my answer is weak, push harder
- After 6 exchanges, step out of character and score me on: clarity, listening, handling objections and securing a next step
- Give me one better line for each answer I struggled with

I'll start: "[your opening line]"

prompts.title: Prompt 7 · Recap the call
prompts.text:
Here are my rough notes from the call with [Name]:
[paste notes or transcript]

Write a recap email that:
1. Thanks them in one line, no fluff
2. Summarizes their situation in their own words (3 bullets max)
3. Lists what we agreed as next steps, with owners and dates
4. Ends with a question to confirm I got it right

Then, separately, give me:
- A 3 line CRM note
- Any open questions or risks I should chase

prompts.title: Quick fix prompt
prompts.text: Review this email against these rules: specific to one buyer, one reason, one question, under 90 words, no buzzwords. Tell me what fails and rewrite only those parts.
